locator.section: 8.3 Steric factors -- hydrogen rearrangements in saturated OE+. ions

evidence.curator_note: EXPERIMENTAL CONTEXT: molecular ion (OE+., n-ionized at oxygen) of cis-4-tert-butylcyclohexanol; page gives no electron energy (electron_energy_ev null, not assumed 70 eV). This is the DISFAVORED (lower) branch of eq 8.26: after the chair-to-boat equilibrium (drawn as an equilibrium arrow, no bond change, not encoded), the reaction arrow leading to the six-membered-TS H-transfer / water-loss product is drawn CROSSED OUT (a large X over the diagonal arrow at lower right). The text states the tertiary H is NOT available for direct transfer via a six-membered transition state in the cis isomer, which eliminates water only to a much lesser extent via a different mechanism. Encoded with support_type=contradicted. Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs on the cis scheme (only the crossed-out reaction arrow); ALL of moves <1,2,3> are reconstructed for electron balance (not drawn on the page) and are identical to the trans transfer in IMS8-EQ8.26a: move <1> O+. odd electron -> forming O-H bond, move <2> one C4-H bonding electron -> forming O-H bond, move <3> the other C4-H bonding electron -> C4 radical. STEREOCHEMISTRY NOT ENCODED: mapped_smiles is the flat connectivity, identical to the trans record; cis vs trans differ only in the relative configuration of OH and tert-butyl, which is exactly the steric factor that blocks this transfer in the cis isomer. This record documents the rejected path only.

locator.section: 8.3 Steric factors -- hydrogen rearrangements in saturated OE+. ions

evidence.curator_note: The inductive (i) C1-O heterolysis / water loss that would follow the H-transfer cannot operate in the cis isomer because its distonic precursor is not formed (the six-membered-TS H-transfer above is crossed out for cis). Encoded with support_type=contradicted to mark the whole facile water-loss pathway as blocked for the cis isomer. Book draws no arc for this step on the cis scheme; the single 2-electron move is reconstructed for electron balance. (The +2 non-bonding electrons on O are a lone pair -- soft lone-pair note from the arrow checker.)
No MOD rule corresponds to equation 8.26 (rule_index by_equation covers chapter 8 only through '8.14'); nothing to cross-link. Consistent with the book crossing this path out for the cis isomer.
